title: Fellowship research brief — Graduate College
text:
Subject: Research brief: Graduate fellowship outcomes and spring mentor call

[Header graphic: Graduate College logo from the 2012 letterhead on an orange and teal banner]

Dear colleagues,

The Graduate College at the University of Illinois at Chicago is pleased to share outcomes from the 2025 Graduate Student Research Fellowship cycle. The fellowship program, which supports doctoral candidates whose dissertation projects cross departmental and disciplinary boundaries, received 214 applications this year, and the review committee, composed of faculty representatives from 11 colleges, recommended awards for 38 students whose proposals demonstrated methodological rigor, feasibility within the funding period and a clear plan for disseminating findings to scholarly and community audiences. Awardees will recieve a stipend supplement and research funds, and each will be paired with a secondary faculty mentor from outside their home department, an arrangement that the the committee believes strengthens interdisciplinary training. Faculty who wish to serve as secondary mentors for the spring cohort should review the expectations document and return the interest form before the deadline.

Mentor interest form: ________ ________ ________

Fellowship guidelines: https//grad.uic.edu/fellowships/2025-guidlines

Regards,
Elaine Porter, PhD
Associate Dean, Graduate College

title: Student Emergency Fund web page — Office of Student Affairs
text:
Student Emergency Fund

The Office of the Dean of Students at the University of Illinois Chicago offers one-time grants to students facing an unexpected financial emergency. Grants can help with rent, utilities, groceries, medical bills or emergency travel.

Who can apply
Students enrolled at least half time who are making SAP and have already used their full COA adjustment through the financial aid office. Students with a pending Title IV disbursement should wait until those funds are released.

Why it matters
In 2014, nearly one in three students at our university reported skipping meals to pay for textbooks.

How to apply
Complete the online application on this page. A case manager will review your request within three business days and contact you by email.

Questions? Visit the Dean of Students office in the Student Services Building, Suite 3030, or call 312-555-0133.

title: Lab safety training policy update — College of Pharmacy
text:
Subject: Updated lab safety training requirement for research personnel

[Sent as a plain-text message; the college research communications template was not used]

Dear colleagues,

Beginning Oct. 15, all faculty, staff and students who work in College of Pharmacy research labs must complete the updated chemical safety training each year. The University of Illinois Chicago Environmental Health and Safety Office has revised the course to include new guidance on handling hazardous drugs and disposing of chemical waste.

Principal investigators are responsible for confirming that everyone in their lab finishes the training by Dec. 1. Lab members who have not completed the course will lose badge access to research spaces until they finish it.

The online course takes about 90 minutes. You can find it in the campus training portal under "Chemical Safety Annual Refresher."

Questions? Contact the college research office at pharmacyresearch@uic.edu or 312-555-0134.

Thank you for helping keep our labs safe.

title: Summer tutoring research brief — College of Education
text:
Research brief: Summer tutoring program narrows reading gaps

A two-year study by researchers in the College of Education at the University of Illinois Chicago found that a summer tutoring program helped elementary students in Chicago Public Schools make measurable gains in reading.

What the study found
Students who attended at least 15 tutoring sessions gained an average of four months of reading growth over the summer. Students in a comparison group showed little change. The largest gains were among students who started the summer reading below grade level.

How the program works
Trained undergraduate tutors meet with small groups of three or four students twice a week. Sessions focus on phonics, vocabulary and reading aloud with a partner. Families receive weekly tips for reading at home.

What comes next
The research team is now working with Chicago Public Schools to expand the program to 12 more schools next summer.

Media contact: College of Education communications, educationnews@uic.edu, 312-555-0109

title: Community dental care annual report — College of Dentistry
text:
Subject: Annual report section: Community dental care

Community dental care

Last year, the College of Dentistry at the University of Illinois Chicago cared for more than 12,000 patients in its community clinics and mobile dental unit.

Our mobile unit visited 48 schools and community centers across Chicago. Dental students, residents and faculty offered free screenings, cleanings and sealants. For many children, it was their first visit to a dentist.

The college also expanded its evening clinic hours. Working adults can now book appointments until 7 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

These programs give our students hands-on training while meeting real needs in the neighborhoods we serve.

Want to partner with our community clinics? Contact our community outreach team at dentistryoutreach@uic.edu or 312-555-0161.
